source.title: Kathleen Writes: Autoregressive Generation and Data Scaling Without Attention

record.tranche_reason: The study measures data scaling and argues that the observed slopes depend on dataset and flatten toward a fixed-capacity ceiling; it also explicitly leaves compute-optimal scaling untested.
record.gate_note: The fixed-parameter byte-level scaling road, its reported slopes, frozen-probe transfer results, and the MELODY perplexity comparison bear on claim versions. Decoding-policy, retrieval, FORM DISTANCE, audio-classification, and scan-speed results do not measure these versions and are not rows. Table 5 repeats results reported in the main text and is not counted as a separate result.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (about 0.5M-parameter attention-free and attention byte-level LMs), the study sweeps training data from 2 to 512 MB at fixed size and reports held-out bits/byte, log-log slopes and their flattening. It also reports frozen-probe downstream accuracy at four pretraining-data scales. It does not argue that any version is wrong, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Within a sub-million-parameter, fixed-size byte-level regime, REVERB beats the parameter-matched attention baseline at every data point. Both curves flatten toward a shared capacity ceiling, and the authors say the probe-transfer plateau reflects the same ceiling. Compute-optimal scaling (growing parameters with data) is left as future work. The paper's other headlines (decoding policy and retrieval dominate generation form) do not concern scaling.
record.recipe_differences: A small fixed-parameter byte-level data sweep with a fixed test slice and two training epochs, rather than a broad parameter, token, and compute scaling study or a compute-optimal allocation sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative log-log slopes vary by dataset: the paper reports REVERB/ATTN slopes of −0.074/−0.107 on WikiText-103 and −0.133/−0.152 on enwik8. It also reports flattening toward a shared fixed-capacity ceiling.

fits_no_version.finding: At near-matched parameter count, the attention-free REVERB beats the ATTN skeleton by 0.20–0.84 bpb at every data size, a ≥16× data-efficiency gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture family (recurrence vs attention) shifts small-model loss substantially at fixed parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: The MELODY FiLM addition (+2.7% params) leaves word-level perplexity unchanged (209 vs 207).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Small architectural add-ons do not change loss at fixed scale.

record.problems: The main scaling road uses one principal corpus, with enwik8 as a smaller robustness check; both datasets are English. Model size is fixed, the attention baseline is the authors' own parameter-matched skeleton rather than a tuned external transformer, and the scaling runs use two seeds. The study does not test parameter or compute scaling, compute-optimal allocation, or small-run extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant outcomes were omitted. Other reported experiments (generation form, retrieval, audio classification, and scan throughput) do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameters and compute; tokenized-token counts; data scaling where model size is not the bottleneck.
Entirely untested. The authors extrapolate a crossover to hundreds of GB but do not check it.
Entirely untested; the authors say the compute-optimal frontier is future work.
Entirely untested; no depth/width/shape sweep at fixed parameter count.
Entirely untested; the audio results are classification accuracy, not loss scaling.
No fit relating downstream accuracy to pretraining loss or scale; only four scales, one seed, two tasks.
Parameter counting, schedule, fitting-method comparisons and compute-optimal split dependence are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Local slopes and matched-range enwik8 comparisons are my calculations from Tables 1 and 3, not reported by the authors. The authors' single slope reproduces as an OLS fit in ln-ln over all five points (-0.0743). The capacity-driven bending is consistent with Kaplan's L(N,D) form, so it qualifies the scope of pure data power laws rather than contradicting V1. Probe accuracies are close to chance, single-seed, with no uncertainty reported.

versions.untested_parts: Only training-data volume is varied, in raw-byte MB, with parameter counts fixed; parameter and compute scaling, tokenized-token counts, and behavior beyond the tested data and capacity range are not tested.
The study reports no predictions made from fits on smaller runs and then checked against substantially larger runs.
The paper explicitly says it does not scale parameters with data or measure the compute-optimal frontier.
Only one architectural addition, MELODY, is compared on perplexity; the study does not sweep depth, width, or a wide range of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The audio results concern classification, not language-model loss scaling in another modality or training regime.
The study reports frozen linear-probe sentiment accuracy at four pretraining-data scales, but does not fit or test a general prediction from pretraining loss to downstream performance.

The study reports dataset-dependent slopes and flattening for fixed-size models; it does not compare published parameter-counting or fitting methods, or test how compute-optimal allocation varies with setup.

relationships.condition: Fixed ~0.5M-param byte-level models, WikiText-103 2–512 MB and enwik8 2–32 MB
relationships.reason: Loss falls monotonically with data (r01–r26), but the log-log curve bends sharply, with local slope about -0.17 to -0.02 computed from Table 1 (r27–r34). A single power law holds over at most about one order of magnitude here; the authors attribute this to the capacity ceiling.
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreased monotonically, but local slopes flattened from about −0.17 to −0.02, limiting a single power law to at most about one decade, which the authors attributed to limited capacity.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Frozen-probe gains over random trunk at 32 MB (REVERB, ATTN) and 512 MB (ATTN)
labels.reason: Table 4 confirms gains in these condition groups: at 32 MB REVERB reaches 64.0/65.8 and ATTN 57.5/63.3 on SST-2/IMDB; ATTN at 512 MB reaches 60.7/62.8, above its random-trunk 54.9/58.4.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.reason: Table 4 shows REVERB declining from 64.0 to 62.5 and 65.8 to 65.2 despite lower pretraining loss; ATTN IMDB at 2 MB is below random, and SST-2 changes from 57.7 to 57.5 over 2–32 MB. Probe seed count is not specified.

relation.reason: The study reports its own data sweeps, fitted slopes, curve flattening and downstream transfer measurements.

tranche.reason: A new small byte-level architecture setting reports data-scaling curves and downstream probes bearing on V7 and V6.

source_check.notes: Architecture baselines are correctly transcribed but are not smaller-data controls. Probe seed counts and uncertainty are unspecified; downstream gains do not establish a quantitative extrapolation law.

statements.correction: REVERB: 565,888 parameters; ATTN: 463,360 parameters. Fixed-size data sweeps flatten; authors attribute flattening to capacity. Non-bottleneck power-law scaling is not established.
statements.problem: The approximately 0.5M-parameter capacity-ceiling description is accurate, but its placement as limits_scope evidence against V1 overlooks V1's existing non-bottleneck qualification.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fixed-size byte-level models over the measured WikiText-103 and enwik8 data ranges
reader_labels.reason: Held-out bits per byte fall as training data increases in the reported points for both architectures; the reported log-log slopes are negative (r01-r30).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Fixed-parameter scaling at the largest measured data sizes
reader_labels.reason: The authors say both curves flatten toward a shared capacity ceiling; the experiment does not establish a power law when model size grows with data (r27-r30).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported perplexity changes from 207 to 209 with a +2.7% parameter increase, which the authors call no gain (r52).

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: Probe accuracy exceeds the corresponding random-trunk value at these scales (r37-r38, r43, r45-r46, r50-r51).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Frozen probes at 512 MB for REVERB and at 2–512 MB for parts of the transfer comparison
reader_labels.reason: REVERB accuracy declines from 32 MB to 512 MB on both tasks, and ATTN IMDB at 2 MB is below its random-trunk control, so transfer is not uniformly monotonic with scale (r39, r41-r42, r47, r49).

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The reported slopes differ across WikiText-103 and enwik8, and the authors describe the relative-slope interpretation as dataset-dependent; they also report flattening toward a capacity ceiling (r27-r30).
